title: Release ramp: staging checklist & metric currency
summary: Working doc that defines the staging-to-production ramp for feature bundles, introduces the notion of 'metric currency' (normalized KPIs across teams), and provides an actionable checklist and gating logic for canaries, rollback, and GA. Intended as a single source for product-ops, engineering, SRE and GTM to align on what constitutes a safe and measurable release ramp.
objective: Standardize the release ramp so that every product bundle passes explicit, measurable gates (quality, performance, cost) in staging and canary before GA. Provide a repeatable checklist that reduces ambiguous 'ready' conversations and short-circuited launches.
scope: Applies to hosted-api feature bundles, console changes with runtime or billing implications, and infra-impacting deploys (Dedicated/Private adjustments). Not a replacement for security or compliance approvals — those are prerequisites handled separately.
milestones: 2025-12-01: Canary widen (25% traffic) if gating passes
2025-12-08: GA approval meeting and final sign-offs
metric_currency_definition: A compact set of normalized KPIs (latency P50/P95/P99, token cost per request, error-rate by code, request success rate, user-facing quality score) converted to a shared scale so product, infra, and GTM can compare tradeoffs. Currency conversions documented here: latency (ms) mapped to 0-100 health score, cost per 1k tokens normalized to cents and mapped to cost-sensitivity buckets.
kpis: Latency P50/P95/P99 — target P95 < 250ms for core endpoints; measured on synthetic and production canary traffic; cadence: 15m aggregated + daily report
Token cost per request — baseline vs optimized path; target: <= 110% of baseline for feature GA; cadence: daily
Error rate (5xx) — target: <= 0.25% on canary; cadence: 5m alerts and hourly trends
Functional correctness (eval passrate) — prompt-suite passrate >= 98% on staging with seeded tests; cadence: on every staging deploy
Customer-impacting incidents during burn-in — target: 0 critical incidents over 72h at 5-25% traffic
control_gates: Gate 1 (Pre-staging): Security/compliance ack present; outstanding high severity bugs = 0; performance budget baseline recorded
Gate 2 (Staging smoke): All automated smoke tests green; functional eval suite >= 98%; service-level synthetic latencies within 120% of baseline
Gate 3 (Staging extended): 48h stability with no critical regressions; metric currency score >= 75/100; load test simulating 1.5x expected canary QPS
Gate 4 (Canary 5%): No SEC/Prod impacting alerts for 24h; error-rate and latency thresholds met; initial user quality metrics acceptable
Gate 5 (Canary 25%): 72h burn-in, monitoring validated, billing/cost analysis reviewed, customer success briefed
Gate 6 (GA): Full checklist complete, cross-functional sign-offs (Product, Eng, SRE, GTM), rollback plan and runbook staged
checklist_items: Create release ticket in Jira with linked PRs and Confluence runbook
Tag release branch and create changelog entry (include customer-visible behavior and known limitations)
Assign on-call + escalation path (Slack channel and pager duty)
Run full staging test matrix (unit, integration, e2e, security scan)
Seed synthetic traffic for latency baselining
Confirm cost signals are being emitted to billing pipeline and cost dashboards
Validate canary routing and fallback policy configured in routing layer
Prepare rollback artifact and tested re-deploy script
Draft customer comms for early adopters and GTM FAQ
Schedule GA approval meeting with stakeholder invite (48h before GA decision)
monitoring_playbook: Dashboards: Release Overview (P50/P95/P99, errors, token cost, traffic split) — owner: SRE
Alerting: Error-rate > 0.25% sustained for 10m = P1; P95 latency > 500ms sustained 10m = P1
Quality monitors: prompt-suite regression diff alerts — owner: Product ML
Cost monitors: daily delta vs baseline > 20% triggers ops review — owner: Finance/Optimize
Tracing: end-to-end trace sample set at 100% for canary traffic to debug regressions — owner: Eng
rollback_triggers: Spike in 5xx errors > 0.5% or sustained > 0.25% for 30m
Critical customer tickets (severity P0/P1) related to the release within canary window
Data correctness failures in evaluation suite (functional regressions > 2%)
Unauthorized access or failed compliance checks detected
capacity_plan: Estimate QPS by region for GA and 1.5x headroom. For Dedicated customers, pre-warm reserved pools 48h before GA and validate autoscaler thresholds in staging. Document GPU memory + batch size matrix for the feature and record projected cost per 1k tokens.
test_matrix: Unit tests — author: owning repo; env: CI
Integration (runtime + kv cache) — author: Eng; env: Staging
Load tests (1.5x expected) — author: Performance team; env: Staging
Prompt-suite regression (seeded) — author: Product ML; env: Staging and Canary
Security scans (SCA/DAST) — author: Security; env: Staging
Billing smoke (token accounting) — author: Finance/Optimize; env: Staging
communication_plan: Weekly internal updates during ramp, daily burn-in summaries while canary >5% traffic. GTM to publish early adopter FAQ 48h before canary. Post-GA retrospective within 2 weeks with key metrics and deviations.
open_questions: Should we require SLOs tightening for all new features or only infra-impacting ones?
Final conversion of metric currency to a single score — is 0-100 acceptable to Eng and Finance?
Do we need an opt-in flag for certain enterprise customers during canary? (legal/privacy implication check)
Who signs off on cost-sensitivity exceptions when a feature increases token cost >15% but improves quality?
notes_for_reviewers: Please focus review on the metric currency mappings and Gate 3 load test targets — these were estimated and need Eng perf sign-off. If you prefer an alternate normalization method for cost vs latency tradeoffs, propose it in PR comments.
